title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers and a target sum.
Find the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target.
Hint: Use a hash map to store seen values for O(n) time complexity.

title: Valid Anagram
description:
Determine if two strings contain the exact same characters in any order.
A classic string manipulation and frequency counting problem.
Hint: Use a hash map or an array of size 26 to count character frequencies.

title: Contains Duplicate
description:
Check if any value appears at least twice in the array.
This is a fundamental problem to test your understanding of sets.
Hint: A hash set will give you O(n) time and space complexity.

title: Group Anagrams
description:
Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together.
You need to find a unique representation for each set of anagrams.
Hint: Sort each string or use character counts as a dictionary key.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description:
Find the k most frequent elements in an integer array.
Tests your ability to use heaps or bucket sort algorithms.
Hint: Count frequencies first, then use a max-heap or bucket array.

title: Valid Palindrome
description:
Check if a string reads the same forwards and backwards.
You should ignore non-alphanumeric characters and case.
Hint: Use two pointers starting from both ends moving towards the center.

title: 3Sum
description:
Find all unique triplets in an array that sum up to zero.
A step up from Two Sum, requiring careful handling of duplicates.
Hint: Sort the array first, then use a loop with two pointers.

title: Container With Most Water
description:
Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container holding the most water.
A classic optimization problem using the two-pointer technique.
Hint: Start pointers at the ends and move the one with the smaller height.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
Calculate how much water can be trapped between elevation maps after raining.
A challenging problem that tests your understanding of arrays and boundaries.
Hint: Use two pointers or precompute the max heights from left and right.

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
description:
Find two numbers that add up to a target in a 1-indexed sorted array.
You must use only constant extra space.
Hint: Since it is sorted, use two pointers from the start and end.

title: Valid Parentheses
description:
Determine if a string of brackets is well-formed and closed in the correct order.
The quintessential stack problem.
Hint: Push opening brackets onto a stack and pop when matching closing brackets.

title: Min Stack
description:
Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time.
Tests your ability to augment standard data structures.
Hint: Store tuples of (value, current_min) in your stack.

title: Daily Temperatures
description:
Find how many days you have to wait until a warmer temperature.
A great introduction to monotonic stacks.
Hint: Keep a stack of indices for temperatures you haven't found a warmer day for.

title: Generate Parentheses
description:
Generate all combinations of n pairs of well-formed parentheses.
A classic backtracking problem.
Hint: Keep track of the number of open and closed brackets you have used.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description:
Find the area of the largest rectangle in a histogram.
A difficult problem that optimally uses a monotonic stack.
Hint: Maintain a stack of indices in increasing order of heights.

title: Binary Search
description:
Find a target integer in a sorted array in O(log n) time.
The foundational algorithm for searching sorted data.
Hint: Maintain left and right pointers and check the middle element.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description:
Find a target in a sorted array that has been pivoted at an unknown point.
Requires modifying the standard binary search logic.
Hint: Determine which half of the array is properly sorted first.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description:
Find the smallest element in a rotated sorted array in O(log n) time.
A variation of binary search focusing on inflection points.
Hint: Compare the middle element with the rightmost element to find the dip.

title: Koko Eating Bananas
description:
Find the minimum eating speed to finish all bananas within h hours.
A classic 'binary search on the answer' problem.
Hint: The minimum speed is 1 and the maximum is the largest pile.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description:
Find the median of two sorted arrays in O(log(m+n)) time.
One of the most challenging binary search problems.
Hint: Binary search on the smaller array to find the correct partition.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description:
Maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy and a single day to sell.
A fundamental problem for sliding window / dynamic programming.
Hint: Keep track of the minimum price seen so far and the max profit.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description:
Find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
The quintessential sliding window problem.
Hint: Use a set or map to track characters in the current window.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description:
Find the minimum window in a string containing all characters of another string.
A hard sliding window problem requiring careful frequency counting.
Hint: Expand the right pointer to find a valid window, then shrink from the left.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description:
Find the longest substring containing the same letter after at most k replacements.
Tests your ability to maintain window state efficiently.
Hint: The window is valid if (length - max_freq_char_count) <= k.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description:
Find the maximum in every sliding window of size k in an array.
A hard problem optimally solved with a deque.
Hint: Maintain a decreasing monotonic queue of indices.

title: Reverse Linked List
description:
Reverse a singly linked list.
The most fundamental linked list manipulation problem.
Hint: Use three pointers: prev, curr, and next.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description:
Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
A classic algorithm that forms the basis of merge sort.
Hint: Use a dummy head node and iteratively attach the smaller node.

title: Linked List Cycle
description:
Determine if a linked list has a cycle in it.
A famous problem testing the slow and fast pointer technique.
Hint: Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm (Tortoise and Hare).

title: Reorder List
description:
Reorder a linked list to alternate between the first and last halves.
Combines finding the middle, reversing a list, and merging.
Hint: Use fast/slow pointers to find the mid, then reverse the second half.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description:
Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
A hard problem that combines linked lists with priority queues.
Hint: Use a min-heap to keep track of the current smallest node among all lists.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description:
Return the level order traversal of a binary tree's nodes' values.
The quintessential Breadth-First Search (BFS) problem for trees.
Hint: Use a queue to process nodes level by level.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description:
Find the maximum depth of a binary tree.
A fundamental Depth-First Search (DFS) or BFS problem.
Hint: The depth is 1 + max(left_depth, right_depth).

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
description:
Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a BST.
Utilizes the core property of Binary Search Trees.
Hint: If both values are greater/less than the root, go right/left.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description:
Find the maximum path sum in a binary tree (any node to any node).
A challenging DFS problem requiring post-order traversal.
Hint: At each node, compute the max path going straight down, but update a global max with the split path.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description:
Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree.
Tests your ability to represent tree structures as strings.
Hint: Pre-order traversal with a special marker for null nodes works well.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description:
Find the kth largest element in an unsorted array.
Can be solved with sorting, heaps, or QuickSelect.
Hint: A min-heap of size k is an optimal solution.

title: K Closest Points to Origin
description:
Find the k closest points to the origin (0, 0).
A classic priority queue problem involving geometry.
Hint: Use a max-heap of size k based on the distance formula.

title: Task Scheduler
description:
Find the minimum intervals required to finish all tasks with a cooldown period.
A tricky greedy/heap problem requiring careful counting.
Hint: Focus on scheduling the most frequent tasks first.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
description:
Design a data structure that supports adding numbers and finding the median.
A hard design problem optimally solved with two heaps.
Hint: Maintain a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description:
Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
A hard problem that combines linked lists with priority queues.
Hint: Use a min-heap to keep track of the current smallest node among all lists.

title: Subsets
description:
Find all possible subsets (the power set) of a unique integer array.
The most basic backtracking/combinatorics problem.
Hint: At each step, you can either include the current element or exclude it.

title: Combination Sum
description:
Find all unique combinations of candidates where the chosen numbers sum to target.
A backtracking problem where elements can be reused.
Hint: Subtract the candidate from the target and recurse.

title: Permutations
description:
Given an array of distinct integers, return all the possible permutations.
A classic backtracking problem for generating all arrangements.
Hint: Swap elements or keep a boolean array of used elements.

title: Word Search
description:
Given a grid of characters, find if a word exists in it (horizontally/vertically).
A standard DFS backtracking problem on a 2D matrix.
Hint: Temporarily modify the board to mark visited cells to avoid revisiting.

title: N-Queens
description:
Place n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other.
The quintessential complex backtracking puzzle.
Hint: Maintain sets for occupied columns, positive diagonals, and negative diagonals.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
description:
Design a Trie data structure supporting insert, search, and startsWith.
The foundational problem for understanding prefix trees.
Hint: Each node should contain an array/map of children and a boolean 'is_end' flag.

title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
description:
Design a data structure that adds words and searches with '.' as a wildcard.
A slightly more complex Trie problem requiring DFS.
Hint: If you encounter a '.', recursively check all possible child nodes.

title: Word Search II
description:
Find all words from a dictionary that are present in a 2D board.
A hard problem combining DFS on a grid with a Trie.
Hint: Build a Trie from the dictionary and traverse the grid, pruning paths not in the Trie.

title: Longest Common Prefix
description:
Find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings.
A straightforward string manipulation problem.
Hint: Compare characters at the same index across all strings until a mismatch occurs.

title: Replace Words
description:
Replace words in a sentence with their shortest root from a dictionary.
An excellent application of a Trie for fast prefix matching.
Hint: Insert all roots into a Trie and find the shortest prefix for each word.

title: Number of Islands
description:
Count the number of islands (connected 1s) in a 2D grid.
The classic graph traversal problem for grids.
Hint: Iterate through the grid and launch a DFS/BFS to sink each island you find.

title: Clone Graph
description:
Return a deep copy of a connected undirected graph.
Tests your ability to traverse graphs and manage object references.
Hint: Use a hash map to map original nodes to their cloned counterparts.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
description:
Find cells where water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans.
A grid traversal problem starting from the boundaries.
Hint: Run DFS/BFS from the ocean borders inwards to find reachable cells.

title: Course Schedule
description:
Determine if you can finish all courses given prerequisite pairs.
A classic topological sort / cycle detection problem.
Hint: Build a directed graph and check for cycles using DFS or Kahn's algorithm.

title: Word Ladder
description:
Find the shortest transformation sequence from a begin word to an end word.
A shortest path problem optimally solved with BFS.
Hint: Build an adjacency list using wildcards (e.g., 'h*t') to connect similar words.

title: Network Delay Time
description:
Find the time it takes for a signal to reach all nodes in a network.
A classic shortest path problem on a weighted graph.
Hint: Use Dijkstra's Algorithm with a min-heap.

title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
description:
Find the minimum cost to connect all points on a 2D plane.
The quintessential Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) problem.
Hint: Use Prim's or Kruskal's algorithm.

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
description:
Find the cheapest price from a source to destination with at most k stops.
A variation of shortest path that adds a constraint on the number of edges.
Hint: Use Bellman-Ford or a modified Dijkstra's/BFS tracking steps.

title: Swim in Rising Water
description:
Find the minimum time needed to reach the bottom-right square of a grid.
A pathfinding problem combining grids and priority queues.
Hint: Use Dijkstra's algorithm, maintaining the max elevation seen on the path.

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
description:
Reconstruct a travel itinerary from a list of airline tickets.
A challenging problem based on finding an Eulerian path.
Hint: Build a graph with sorted destinations and do a post-order DFS.

title: Climbing Stairs
description:
Find the number of distinct ways to climb n stairs taking 1 or 2 steps.
The 'Hello World' of dynamic programming.
Hint: The solution is identical to computing the Fibonacci sequence.

title: House Robber
description:
Find the maximum amount of money you can rob from houses without robbing adjacent ones.
A fundamental 1D dynamic programming problem.
Hint: At each house, you decide to either rob it (plus dp[i-2]) or skip it (dp[i-1]).

title: Coin Change
description:
Find the minimum number of coins needed to make up a given amount.
A classic unbounded knapsack problem.
Hint: Build up the solution from amount 0 up to the target amount.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description:
Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in an array.
A core dynamic programming concept that can also be solved with binary search.
Hint: dp[i] represents the length of the LIS ending at index i.

title: Word Break
description:
Determine if a string can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of dictionary words.
A 1D DP problem testing string matching and state.
Hint: dp[i] is true if the string up to index i can be segmented.

title: Unique Paths
description:
Find the number of possible unique paths from top-left to bottom-right of a grid.
The fundamental 2D dynamic programming problem.
Hint: The number of paths to a cell is the sum of paths to the cell above it and left of it.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description:
Find the length of the longest common subsequence between two strings.
A classic 2D DP problem comparing two sequences.
Hint: Build a 2D DP table where dp[i][j] represents the LCS up to indices i and j.

title: Edit Distance
description:
Find the minimum operations to convert one string to another.
A famous DP problem used in spell checkers and genetics.
Hint: Operations are insert, delete, and replace. Map them to your DP transitions.

title: Burst Balloons
description:
Find the maximum coins you can collect by bursting balloons.
A very challenging DP problem that requires thinking in reverse.
Hint: dp[i][j] represents the max coins obtained by bursting balloons between i and j.

title: Regular Expression Matching
description:
Implement regular expression matching with support for '.' and '*'.
A difficult string parsing problem optimally solved with 2D DP.
Hint: Carefully handle the '*' character, which can represent zero or more of the preceding element.

title: Jump Game
description:
Determine if you can reach the last index of an array.
A classic greedy problem.
Hint: Keep track of the maximum reachable index as you iterate.

title: Jump Game II
description:
Find the minimum number of jumps to reach the last index.
A greedy problem requiring you to track the current jump boundaries.
Hint: Maintain the farthest index reachable in the current jump and the next jump.

title: Gas Station
description:
Find the starting gas station's index if you can travel around the circuit once.
A greedy problem that requires single-pass optimization.
Hint: If total gas >= total cost, a solution exists. Keep track of the current tank deficit.

title: Partition Labels
description:
Partition a string into as many parts as possible so each letter appears in at most one part.
A greedy problem involving character last-occurrence indices.
Hint: Record the last occurrence of each character, then iterate and update the partition boundary.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
description:
Find the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest non-overlapping.
A greedy interval scheduling problem.
Hint: Sort by end times and always pick the interval that ends earliest.

title: Merge Intervals
description:
Merge all overlapping intervals into an array of non-overlapping intervals.
The foundational problem for interval manipulation.
Hint: Sort intervals by start time and merge if the next start <= current end.

title: Insert Interval
description:
Insert a new interval into a list of non-overlapping intervals and merge if necessary.
A slightly trickier interval problem requiring careful ordering.
Hint: Iterate and handle three cases: entirely before, entirely after, or overlapping.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
description:
Find the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest non-overlapping.
A greedy interval scheduling problem.
Hint: Sort by end times and always pick the interval that ends earliest.

title: Meeting Rooms
description:
Determine if a person could attend all meetings (no overlapping intervals).
A basic interval scheduling problem.
Hint: Sort the intervals by start time and check if any start time is less than the previous end time.

title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query
description:
Find the size of the smallest interval containing each query point.
A challenging problem combining intervals, sorting, and priority queues.
Hint: Sort queries and intervals. Use a min-heap to keep track of valid interval sizes.

title: Single Number
description:
Find the single element in an array where every other element appears twice.
A classic bit manipulation trick problem.
Hint: XOR all elements together; duplicates will cancel each other out.

title: Number of 1 Bits
description:
Write a function that takes an unsigned integer and returns the number of '1' bits.
A fundamental bitwise operations test.
Hint: Use the trick n & (n - 1) to clear the lowest set bit.

title: Counting Bits
description:
Return an array of the number of 1's in the binary representation of numbers from 0 to n.
A DP problem based on bit manipulation.
Hint: The number of bits for n is the number of bits for n/2 plus n % 2.

title: Reverse Bits
description:
Reverse the bits of a 32-bit unsigned integer.
A bit manipulation problem requiring shifting and masking.
Hint: Extract bits one by one and shift them into the reversed result.

title: Sum of Two Integers
description:
Calculate the sum of two integers without using the operators + and -.
A computer architecture problem simulating an adder with bitwise logic.
Hint: Use XOR for addition without carry, and AND with left shift for the carry.

title: Rotate Image
description:
Rotate an n x n 2D matrix 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
A tricky matrix manipulation problem.
Hint: First transpose the matrix (swap symmetry), then reverse each row.

title: Spiral Matrix
description:
Return all elements of an m x n matrix in spiral order.
A simulation problem requiring careful boundary management.
Hint: Keep track of top, bottom, left, and right boundaries and shrink them as you go.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
description:
If an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0 in-place.
A matrix problem requiring space optimization.
Hint: Use the first row and first column to keep track of which rows and columns need to be zeroed.

title: Happy Number
description:
Determine if a number is 'happy' (sum of squares of digits eventually reaches 1).
A math and cycle detection problem.
Hint: Use a hash set to track seen numbers, or Floyd's Cycle-Finding Algorithm.

title: Pow(x, n)
description:
Calculate x raised to the power n.
A math problem requiring an efficient O(log n) algorithm.
Hint: Use binary exponentiation: x^n = (x^2)^(n/2).
